summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Phramonchai Saitanaporn completed a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, having also studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.

Phrapongsak K. is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held positions in 2015 as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Phuntsok Tashi earned a BA from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff earned degrees from Radcliffe College and Harvard University. A scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, she was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and became Lex Hixon Professor of World Religions at Yale University in 2004.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies, Pierce Salguero studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins. He held positions at Pennsylvania State University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Penn State Abington (~2012).
Pierre Arènes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under André Bareau. He held a post at the CNRS (attested 2003–2004).

Philosopher Pierre Bourdieu studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University of Science and Technology, the EHESS, and the Collège de France (1981–2001).
Linguist Pierre Chantraine studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes (~1920–1927). He served as a professor at the University of Paris from circa 1938 to 1969.

Indologist and linguist Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat worked at the French Institute of Pondicherry and EFEO (1963–1967). He held the Sanskrit Chair at the EPHE (1967–2004), was Vice-President of the Société Asiatique (2000–2019), and became President of the AIBL in 2010.
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Leiden University by 1991 and served there as a research fellow (attested 1996).
Pieter Hendrik Pott worked in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Museum Volkenkunde (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

Pietro Merlo studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia in 1867. He taught at the University of Pavia from 1877, becoming extraordinary professor in 1880 and full professor of comparative linguistics in 1885.

Indologist and philosopher Piotr Balcerowicz studied at Warsaw, Banaras Hindu, and Hamburg universities. He has served as professor at the University of Warsaw since circa 2000, SWPS University (2008–2011), and held visiting professorships at Hamburg, Munich, Punjab, and Ashoka.

Piotr Klafkowski was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University under Jerzy Bańczerowski and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.
Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Palzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka worked in linguistics, Indology, and archaeology, studying at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He worked at Dinas Purbakala and later held professorships at Gadjah Mada University, the University of Indonesia, and Udayana University.

Polly Young-Eisendrath earned degrees from Goddard College and Washington University in St. Louis, and trained under Philip Kapleau and Shinzen Young. In 1994, she became clinical associate professor in psychiatry at the University of Vermont.

Active in Indology and history and archaeology, Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad served as State Engineer in Junagadh, Chief Engineer for Jodhpur State, and Chief Officer and Engineer for Hyderabad Municipality.
Pori Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Robert Buswell. She held a position as assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Potprecha Cholvijarn studied at Chulalongkorn University and the University of Bristol, where he completed doctoral research under Rupert Gethin. He worked in Buddhist and religious studies and served as a special lecturer at Chulalongkorn University (attested 2011).
